title: Mergeable by default: Building the context engine to save time and tokens — Peter Werry, Unblocked
talk_summary: Peter Werry of Unblocked argues that agents fail not from lack of access but lack of understanding, and describes a 'context engine' that distills PR comments, Slack, and code history into memories, expert graphs, and conflict resolution. He reports a large task dropping from 2.5h/21M tokens to 25min/10M tokens with the engine, and gives concrete lessons on what not to build.

takeaways.technique: Distill PR review comments into reusable 'memories'
takeaways.what_they_do: They mine historical PR comments, distill repeated patterns into memories, and load them when an agent works on similar code so it follows org best practices.

takeaways.technique: Seed context up front rather than let agent search
takeaways.what_they_do: They inject high-signal seed context (expert context, memories) before the agent runs, because agents otherwise burn tokens searching and stop at the first plausible hit ('satisfaction of search').
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't really leave it up to the agent to do memory hydration because that's kind of like part of the seed context
takeaways.numbers: 2.5h/21M tokens without engine vs 25min/10M tokens with

takeaways.what_they_do: Their reviewer flags issues grounded in distilled best practices from past PRs, not just local code correctness, and cites references back to the author.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this was a best practice that was distilled from a bunch of other PRs

takeaways.technique: Don't cache answers; surface unresolved conflicts
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly warn against caching context-engine answers or feeding prior answers back as context, and against silently resolving conflicts with recency/code heuristics; unresolved conflicts are surfaced to humans and learned from.
takeaways.evidence_quote: do not cache the answer and try to serve that same answer up again... you regress towards the mean

takeaways.technique: Ticket enrichment and triage via context engine
takeaways.what_they_do: They use the context engine at planning time (biggest ROI) to enrich new tickets with relevant history and to triage production issues against past incidents and Slack discussions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: during the planning phase... This is where you get the biggest bang for buck unquestionably

takeaways.what_they_do: They build a contributor graph from PR review relationships to identify area experts, then use 'bottling the expert' (distilled history of that person's decisions) as a jump point for retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: understanding who the experts are in a particular code area acts as a jump point
